newsitem.title: USA: TECH RALLY TAKES BREAK, NASDAQ SLIPS SLIGHTLY.
newsitem.headline: TECH RALLY TAKES BREAK, NASDAQ SLIPS SLIGHTLY.

text.p: Nasdaq shares took a breather Thursday, snapping a six-day winning streak, as investors took profits amid weakness in the bond market, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index lost 6.26 points or 0.39 percent to close unofficially at 1624.16. Declining issues only slightly beat gainers, 2209 to 2149, on heavy volume of 753.8 million shares.

"After the run the techs had, it makes sense that they would take a break. It was hard to continue those gains for a week straight, especially with the Dow off and the bond market off," one trader said. The Dow industrials slipped 71 points to 8188, while the benchmark 30-year treasury bond dropped 20/32 to yield 6.56 percent.

Bellwether technology stocks had a mixed performance, but Apple Computer Inc continued to rise after Wednesday's announcement that Microsoft Corp agreed to invest $150 million in the struggling computer maker. Apple gained 2-14/16 to 29-3/16.
In other news, HMO stocks suffered and retailer Wet Seal Inc dropped 29 percent after it said it expects its second quarter earnings and revenues to be flat compared to year- ago performance.
